properties.snippet: This innovative Web GIS tool powered by ESRI’s ArcGIS Online is designed to empower communities and developers by providing easy access to crucial data for energy planning and development. As Kansas transitions towards a more sustainable energy future, this tool will be an invaluable resource for local governments and communities, planners, and developers.
properties.description:
The energy transition landscape in the United States has over the recent years been dominated by a fast-paced growth in Renewable Energy developments but even more important is the growth in opposition to this transition. The United States has set a target to achieve 100% clean energy by 2035 and Net Zero ( Zero carbon emissions) by 2050. This calls for significant investments in renewable energy generation in the country especially in Wind and Solar which have the potential to offset the dependence on fossil fuels. However, the policy landscape in the US is characterized by a 3-tiered systems of government regulations with the addition of 1 more considering the Indigenous nations. The regulatory environment consists of the federal level, state level and county level. The federal level policies have in recent years provided a conducive environment for renewables , the state have had mixed approaches for and against renewables and even more impactful is the county governments which can block or enable the deployment of the renewable systems. This multilayered system of regulation has made it difficult for developers navigating the regulatory environments. Recent reports such as the Survey of Utility scale Wind and Solar developers 2023, indicated that the primary cause of renewable energy development cancellations and delays was local regulations / ordinances.
 
For communities, the Atlas offers comprehensive data to inform energy planning regulations, ensuring that decisions are based on the latest and most accurate information. This will help in crafting policies that promote sustainable energy practices and meet the unique needs of each community.
 
 
For developers, the tool provides detailed insights and data necessary for crafting development proposals. By leveraging this information, developers can create projects that align with local regulations and contribute to the state’s energy goals.
 
The full Kansas geospatial catalog is administered by the Kansas Data Access & Support Center (DASC) and can be found at the following URL: https://hub.kansasgis.org/

properties.snippet: This data layer shows locations and related information for underground natural gas storage fields in Kansas. The original dataset was created to identify and provide detailed information on underground natural gas storage in the United States.
properties.description:
This data layer shows locations and related information for underground natural gas storage fields in Kansas. This layer is intended for general reference and includes both active and inactive fields. The EIA-191 Monthly Underground Gas Storage Report was a source used to improve location accuracy.  Other sources include Homeland Infrastructure Foundation-Level Data (HIFLD), EPA Facility Registry Service (FRS), National Pipeline Mapping System Public Viewer, company websites, and satellite imagery. 

The Kansas Geological Survey clipped the original data to the state of Kansas. The Monthly Underground Gas Storage Report contains the most current data.

properties.snippet: The purpose of this information is to provide a regularly updated, publicly available, spatially referenced, national dataset made up almost entirely of utility-scale wind turbine locations and their technical specifications. An appropriate use of the data would be for scientific analysis, research or for general interest for the public. Identification of turbines that have been retrofitted, repowered, decommissioned, and/or removed is a continual ongoing effort; thus, the dataset may contain turbines that were previously verified and subsequently removed.
properties.description: This dataset provides locations and technical specifications of wind turbines in the United States, almost all of which are utility-scale. Utility-scale turbines are ones that generate power and feed it into the grid, supplying a utility with energy. They are usually much larger than turbines that would feed a homeowner or business. The regularly updated database has wind turbine records that have been collected, digitized, and locationally verified. Turbine data were gathered from the Federal Aviation Administration's (FAA) Digital Obstacle File (DOF) and Obstruction Evaluation Airport Airspace Analysis (OE-AAA), the American Wind Energy Association (AWEA), Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory (LBNL), and the United States Geological Survey (USGS), and were merged and collapsed into a single data set. Verification of the turbine positions was done by visual interpretation using high-resolution aerial imagery in ESRI ArcGIS Desktop. A locational error of plus or minus 10 meters for turbine locations was tolerated. Technical specifications for turbines were assigned based on the wind turbine make and models as provided by manufacturers and project developers directly, and via FAA datasets, information on the wind project developer or turbine manufacturer websites, or other online sources. Some facility and turbine information on make and model did not exist or was difficult to obtain. Thus, uncertainty may exist for certain turbine specifications. Similarly, some turbines were not yet built, not built at all, or for other reasons cannot be verified visually. Location and turbine specifications data quality are rated and a confidence is recorded for both. None of the data are field verified.

properties.snippet: Oil and gas leases in Kansas. These points represent areas where landowners have leased mineral rights for exploration, drilling, and production of oil and gas.
properties.description:
An oil and/or gas lease is an agreement between a mineral owner (lessor) and a company (lessee) in which the owner grants the company the right to explore, drill and produce oil, gas, and other minerals below the surface of the earth. Oil and gas leases are created so that property owner can maintain their mineral rights while leasing their land to an extraction company.

The Kansas Geological Survey maintains and publishes this GIS data. The Kansas Department of Revenue is the data originator, and they send updates to the KGS monthly.

properties.snippet: This data layer shows oil and gas wells in Kansas. The data is for use by citizens and companies interested in the oil and gas resources of the state.
properties.description:
This is GIS data of well-header information for oil and gas wells in Kansas. The data is based on well information submitted to the Kansas Corporation Commission on wells planned, drilled, worked over, or plugged. Well information is also collected from wireline logs, core or cuttings submitted for storage, or historical compilations. Some data from other states is included for research purposes. The Kansas Geological Survey compiles and publishes this data. For field/column definitions, download this spreadsheet.

The Kansas Geological Survey works with the Kansas Corporation Commission and the Kansas Department of Revenue to create an accurate list of the oil and gas wells in Kansas. While the other agencies have regulatory duties facilitated by having an accurate accounting of oil and gas wells, the Survey maintains the list for research purposes and for use by citizens and companies interested in the oil and gas resources of the state.

properties.snippet: This layer shows oil and gas wells in Kansas that were part of the Type Logs Project. Log ASCII Standard (LAS) 3.0 files are available for these wells.
properties.description: This data layer shows locations of oil and gas wells that were designated to be part of the Type Logs Project, which created extended data for wells. Some of the extended data includes the well tops for each well and the owner of the tops, the result of the Type Log Committee evaluation of the tops, the Stratigraphic Units for the Type Log Project & CO2 Project, the Committee members for the Type Log Project who selected and evaluated the tops, and LAS 3.0 files. The type LAS 3.0 file includes the final files containing the Log Data, Tops Data, and, if present, the Geologist Report Data. These files are part of the final deliverables for the Type Log Project and are also part of the CO2 Project mapper program to allow users to build General Cross Sections. This project was conducted by the Energy Research Department of the Kansas Geological Survey.
